name: upgrade_pydantic_orm_mode_to_from_attributes
description: Migrate pydantic 1.x class Config: orm_mode=True + .from_orm() to 2.x model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True) + .model_validate() - the unmigrated code raises PydanticUserError immediately (from_orm requires from_attributes=True); incomplete-fix broken updates the call site to model_validate() but forgets to set from_attributes=True, so validating a plain (non-dict, non-model) object raises a ValidationError
prompts: This project is being upgraded from pydantic 1.x to pydantic 2.x (the version actually installed and imported by `import pydantic` in this sandbox - you can check the old behavior against a real pydantic 1.10 install at /opt/venv-pydantic1/bin/python if useful, but the code you write must work under the installed pydantic 2.x). UserOut in user_out.py uses the pydantic 1.x `class Config: orm_mode = True` plus `UserOut.from_orm(row)` pattern to build a UserOut from an arbitrary object with matching attributes (not a dict, not already a UserOut - e.g. a database row object). Under the installed pydantic 2.x, calling `.from_orm()` without `from_attributes=True` set raises a PydanticUserError immediately. Migrate to the pydantic 2.x pattern: `model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True)` as a class attribute, and use `UserOut.model_validate(row)` instead of `.from_orm(row)` in to_user_out(). Preserve the exact behavior: to_user_out(row) returns a UserOut built from row's id and name attributes.

test_setup_files.test_user_out.py:
from user_out import to_user_out


class UserRow:
    def __init__(self, id, name):
        self.id = id
        self.name = name


row = UserRow(1, "Ada")
out = to_user_out(row)
assert out.id == 1 and out.name == "Ada", f"unexpected result: {out}"

print("PASS")
